origin.description: The new index must have the same length. index<- rejects it unless ORDER(value) is 1 through n, so it must already be sorted and a missing value must already be last. On a zooreg, a spacing that no longer divides the frequency drops that frequency.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object. A zoo series stores observations separately from its index.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A new index of the same length. It must already be in order.

origin.details: The new index must have the same length. index<- rejects it unless ORDER(value) is 1 through n, so it must already be sorted and a missing value must already be last. On a zooreg, a spacing that no longer divides the frequency drops that frequency.
origin.value: The series with the new index.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(1:4, 1:4)
index(x) <- c(2, 3, 4, 5)
cat(paste(index(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.value: The series with the new index.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.index import index, index_set
x = index_set(Zoo(np.arange(1, 5), [1, 2, 3, 4]), [2, 3, 4, 5])
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in index(x)))
